explanation:
The only mismatch is the 8 bar hugging the right wall in pair 1: input cells (10,15),(11,15),(12,15). My shift puts it at rows 12–14, but the expected output has 8 in rows 10–14 — the bar's old position is kept as well as its new one, so the object effectively stretches down to the border rather than sliding. Every other object (including the 2 bar on the right wall in pair 2, which slides from rows 6–7 up to rows 1–2) moves cleanly.

What singles this bar out: it is pressed against a side wall *and* its destination overlaps its original footprint (shift 2, height 3). The pair-2 wall bar has shift 5 with height 2, so no overlap, and it slides. The 9 bar at x=5 in pair 1 also overlaps its destination (shift 2, height 3) but is not on a wall, and it slides. So the exception I encode is: an object touching a side wall whose shifted copy overlaps its original position keeps the union of both (it stretches to the border). In the test input the wall-touching objects — the 1 at (5,0) and the 4 corner at (8–9, 14–15) — move far enough that no overlap occurs, so they simply slide like everything else.

def transform(grid):
    g = np.array(grid)
    H, W = g.shape
    bg = background(g)
    top_c = g[0, 0]
    bot_c = g[H - 1, 0]

    out = g.copy()
    interior = np.zeros_like(g, dtype=bool)
    interior[1:H - 1, :] = True
    mask_top = (g == top_c) & interior
    mask_bot = (g == bot_c) & interior
    out[mask_top | mask_bot] = bg
    emit(out.copy(), "Erase every interior shape of the two border colours; they will be re-placed against their own border row.")

    def place(comp, shift, colour):
        touches_wall = any(x == 0 or x == W - 1 for y, x in comp)
        orig = set(comp)
        moved = {(y + shift, x) for y, x in comp}
        cells = moved
        if touches_wall and (orig & moved):
            # wall-hugging object whose new position overlaps the old one stretches instead of sliding
            cells = orig | moved
        for y, x in cells:
            out[y, x] = colour

    for comp in components(mask_top, diagonal=True):
        y0 = min(y for y, x in comp)
        shift = 1 - y0
        place(comp, shift, top_c)
        emit(out.copy(), f"Move a colour-{top_c} object up so its top touches row 1 (shift {shift}).")

    for comp in components(mask_bot, diagonal=True):
        y1 = max(y for y, x in comp)
        shift = (H - 2) - y1
        place(comp, shift, bot_c)
        emit(out.copy(), f"Move a colour-{bot_c} object down so its bottom touches row {H-2} (shift {shift}).")

    emit(out.copy(), "All shapes rest against the border row of their own colour.")
    return out
